entries.title: Swiss Cultural Poster System
entries.why: A durable poster reference for high-contrast hierarchy, disciplined whitespace, and type-led cultural communication without decorative overload.

entries.title: Munich 1972 Sports Poster System
entries.maker: Otl Aicher and Munich 1972 design team
entries.why: A benchmark for turning a large event identity into a disciplined but lively poster family: consistent color, photographic treatment, pictogram logic, and event metadata work together without flattening each sport.

entries.title: The Public Theater Typographic Poster Language
entries.why: A strong reference for using typography as the image itself: bold condensed type, sharp figure-ground contrast, and city-like pacing create posters that feel immediate without depending on complex illustration.

compositions.title: Oversized type as image
compositions.study: Large type carries the visual mass while smaller metadata locks to a strict axis.
compositions.reuse: Use when a poster needs authority and quick distance readability.

compositions.title: Asymmetric grid tension
compositions.study: Composition feels dynamic because text blocks are offset inside a rigorous grid.
compositions.reuse: Use for event posters, conference visuals, and cultural announcements.

compositions.title: Sport-by-sport color family
compositions.study: Each poster can stand alone while sharing a repeated image treatment, controlled palette, and consistent Olympic information zone.
compositions.reuse: Use when an event needs many sub-posters that must feel collectible but unmistakably related.

compositions.title: Posterized action with quiet metadata
compositions.study: High-energy athletic imagery is reduced into graphic planes while title and mark remain calm and systemized.
compositions.reuse: Use for sports, festival, conference-track, or product-feature series where motion needs to become a static signal.

compositions.entryTitle: The Public Theater Typographic Poster Language
compositions.title: Type as the performing subject
compositions.study: Large sans-serif typography carries emotional force while image fragments provide context and tempo.
compositions.reuse: Use when a poster needs voice, urgency, and cultural confidence before image detail is read.

compositions.entryTitle: The Public Theater Typographic Poster Language
compositions.title: Institution identity through campaign variation
compositions.study: The theater identity stays recognizable while each production gets a distinct typographic arrangement.
compositions.reuse: Use for annual programs, performing arts calendars, or editorial series that need continuity with room for expression.

assets.notes: Use original typography choices; do not copy source lettering.
assets.reuse: Build a fresh type scale and lockup from the observed hierarchy.

assets.notes: Palette should be compact and high contrast.
assets.reuse: Reserve one accent for event identity or callout information.

assets.notes: Color identifies entries inside the system without needing a new layout each time.
assets.reuse: Define a small palette and reserve one family of colors for the series grammar.

assets.notes: Action photography is treated as graphic material rather than documentary illustration.
assets.reuse: Convert motion into bold silhouettes, rhythm, or tonal blocks using original or licensed imagery.

assets.entryTitle: The Public Theater Typographic Poster Language
assets.notes: Condensed, stacked, and cropped type can create a loud public signal without adding decoration.
assets.reuse: Build a fresh typographic system with controlled compression, weight contrast, and axis shifts.

assets.entryTitle: The Public Theater Typographic Poster Language
assets.notes: Simple image fragments support the type instead of competing with it.
assets.reuse: Use one strong supporting crop or silhouette after the type hierarchy is working.
